chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Sama'ah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Do not rent the land for wheat, nor for barley, nor for dates, nor for four qirats, nor for two qirats, but rent it for gold and silver, because gold and silver are guaranteed (liable for loss), whereas these [crops] are not guaranteed."

key_terms.النِّطَاف: A smaller weight unit (two qirats), also used for grain.
key_terms.الْأَرْبِعَاء: A weight unit (four qirats), used here as a metonym for grain/crops.
key_terms.مُزَارَعَة: Agricultural partnership where one party provides land and the other labor, sharing the crop.

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method of payment for land rental in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to resolve the ambiguity of risk in agricultural partnerships by mandating fixed monetary payment rather than variable crop yields. This ensures contractual certainty (*daman*), as gold and silver retain their intrinsic value and are liable for return even if lost, unlike perishable crops which carry inherent uncertainty (*gharar*). This principle underpins the Shia jurisprudence of *muzara'ah*, prioritizing financial stability over speculative agricultural returns.
